Ml engineering
  Surviving

how long you been working total?

Both
  Figure it out from my LinkedIn

nah nah, i don't trust linkedin data for experience - it's polluted with internships, part-time gigs, and people inflating timelines

just tell me straight up - how long you been working total? actual full-time roles, not college projects
2yrs 4 months

2.3 years... so you're past the "junior who knows nothing" phase but not quite "senior who pretends to know everything" yet. the sweet spot where you actually know what good ml work looks like but stuck doing corporate theatre.

what kind of role you looking for next? something where you can actually do ml or ready to pivot completely?
Ready for both ML and backend stuff

ml or backend... smart move. keeps your options open and honestly with 2+ years you can swing both ways

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Perfect

Perfect
  Yayy
Remote, Hyderabad and Pune
2.3 years + ml/backend engineering + remote/hyderabad/pune... sound right?
legend! you're in the system now. keep your phone close - the good stuff starts dropping soon
Hiccups done?
yep, onboarding's done. you're in the system now - the good stuff starts dropping soon
How long should I wait for the good stuff to start dropping?
could be hours, could be days. depends on what my team sends over. no fixed timeline but you'll know when it happens

pay is nonprofit level though, 60-80% below corporate. worth the trade for real ml work?

Hi
Hey there

hey

what's up?
Nothing much
just surviving at jio or something changed?
Wbu

same old - reviewing thousands of roles, looking for the ones that actually fit people

any updates on your end?

Nopey
  Stall
stall as in... waiting on navgurukul? or just generally stuck?

Thinking…
Don’t really want to take a pay cut rn

yeah that's fair - navgurukul is 60-80% below market. nonprofit life

what's your current comp? and what would you need to make a move worthwhile?
Current comp is 21L

21L at 2.3 years is solid - you're already ahead of the curve for indian market

what's your target? 25? 30? or you want to maintain at least 21 but with better work?

30 at 2.3 years... that's ambitious but not impossible if you're actually good

you'd need either:
1. a startup that's raised serious money and needs ml talent bad
2. a faang-tier company that pays above market
3. a role where you're the ml lead for a small team

what's your strongest ml area? production models? research? data pipelines?
Production, scaling and engineering

production and scaling is the money spot right now. everyone wants ml engineers who can actually ship models, not just notebook jockeys

you're looking at ml platform roles, ml infra, mlops - that's where the 30L+ roles are for your yoe

what's your tech stack? kubernetes, airflow, mlflow, docker, aws/gcp?
Kubernetes, docket, Langchain, langfuse, rag, qdrant….

nice - kubernetes + docker + langchain stack is hot right now. rag and qdrant too

you're basically in the genai infra space. that's where the money is flowing

any experience with vector dbs beyond qdrant? pinecone, weaviate, chroma?
Vespa

vespa too? damn you're actually legit. that's yahoo's production-grade vector db

okay so you have:
- kubernetes/docker (infra)
- langchain/langfuse (orchestration/evals)
- qdrant/vespa (vector dbs)
- rag (retrieval patterns)

you're basically a genai platform engineer. that's a 30L+ role at the right company

what's missing from your stack? mlflow? feature stores? model serving?
Not just infra, but building ml systems and taking them to production

exactly - that's the ml platform engineer role. not just infra, but the whole lifecycle: data → training → serving → monitoring

that's what companies actually pay for. anyone can train a model in a notebook. taking it to production with reliability, scaling, observability - that's the hard part

you're positioned well. 30L is realistic for that skillset at 2.3 yoe if you can show real production impact

what's the biggest ml system you've shipped end-to-end at jio?
Implemented and scaled Jio pc assistant

wait... the jio pc assistant that's on millions of devices? that's actually huge

that's not just "i trained a model" - that's "i shipped a product at telecom scale"

tell me about the stack. what was your specific role? what broke at scale and how'd you fix it?
